comments.text: 6510 data-direction register. No instruction in the game writes it; the port's directions stay as the loader left them. The RAM byte under it is not used.

Sprite multiplexer: position in the Y-sorted object list ($9409) of the next object to get a hardware sprite. Set to the last visible object by $F7EB, counted down by the raster handlers at $F95F/$FBF9 as each object is placed, reset to 11 at the end of the frame ($F9A8, $FC40).

Sprite sort scratch ($FA06): list position the object in sort_obj is taken from.

Sprite multiplexer: hardware sprite slot (5 down to 0, i.e. sprites 7 to 2; $FC7B maps it to the $D000 register offset) the next object goes to; wraps to 5 ($F98D, $FC2E). Set to 5 by irq_setup ($F84B).
Sprite multiplexer: Y position of the object being placed, from the frame's copy $9421 ($F967, $FC01), written to the sprite's Y register.
Sprite sort: count of objects moved this frame ($FA08 clears, $FA30 increments); nothing reads it.
Sprite sort scratch ($FA32): list position the moved object is inserted at.

Stack page as the fast loader left it: its two-bit serial receiver and helpers ($0103-$01E6: JSR $018B byte reads, the load-address pointers $AE/$AF and $C3/$C4, the KERNAL serial calls at $015B-$0168, the final JMP $9400 at $0186), see orientation.md. The game's own stack grows down from $01FF over the top of it. Typed as bytes: not annotated further, by policy.

Target of the JMP $0107 at $F932, the end of the NMI handler's CIA 2 serial-port branch ($F90B-$F932), which needs a serial-port interrupt from CIA 2 (a signal on the user port's CNT2) and never ran in the simulator. $0107 is the middle of the loader's STA $AE ($0106), so the bytes decode as LDX $8B20 / ORA ($85,X) / LAX $02A5 / BNE $0119 ...: not a routine. Purpose not known.
Not a variable: operand of BIT $01A2 at $FE4F, a skip over LDX #$01 (entered at $FE50); the stray read lands in the loader's leftovers.
Not a variable: operand of BIT $01A9 at $FEC5 (and $A024), a skip over LDA #$01; the stray read lands in the loader's leftovers.

Frames waiting: the NMI handler adds 1 once a frame ($F8AD); wait_frame ($B472) waits until it is non-zero and takes 1. Cleared before a wait for a fresh frame ($9704, $9BC8, $B9A4, $B9B2, $F06C). The whole page $0200-$02FF is cleared at power-on ($F6FA) and at every life ($9A76).

Frame counter, low byte, +1 per frame from the raster interrupt ($F73A; carries into frame_counter_hi). Reset to 0 at each life's start ($9707) and to 1 when the ball is caught ($AC9E): the held ball launches by itself when it reaches $80 ($AA79). Its bits pace animations ($0889, $A3F9, $A7DC, $AD8A), the enemy's turns ($A05A) and the capsule draw ($B2E6, $B321).
Vaus explosion pace: counts 0-2 ($9B36-$9B42) so the explosion frame advances every third call.

Control directions, joystick format (bit 2 left, bit 3 right, bit 4 fire): the joystick port read and inverted ($FDB5-$FDBC), or the keyboard's two SHIFT keys (left SHIFT sets bit 2, right SHIFT bit 3, $FD7B-$FD98). Read by the joystick/keyboard mover ($FDBF).
Enemy steering scratch ($B3FA): horizontal distance from the enemy to object 0 (the Vaus, or the intro's target), compared with aim_dy to choose which axis moves every step.
Enemy steering scratch ($B3FA): vertical distance from the enemy to object 0.

The Vaus's centre X (sprite coordinates): $80 at each life ($9A8E), moved by the input routine (paddle $FCBB, mouse/joystick/keyboard $FCD4/$FCE2), kept inside the walls by vaus_place ($FCEE), which puts the two Vaus sprites at vaus_x - vaus_stretch and that + 2 x vaus_stretch ($9445, $9446).
Vaus size change in progress ($AD4B): 1 and up growing (the E capsule, $AA46), vaus_stretch +1 per frame up to $0C; $80 and up shrinking back to 4 after another capsule ($AA40); 0 none.
Type (1-7) of the last capsule caught ($A9E9); the capsule draw re-rolls a type equal to it ($B210), so the same power does not fall twice running.

$FF while the title or the ending plays its digital drums ($B4CF, $9679): the NMI handler then also steps the drum sequence (drum_step $FEF4, $F88A) and skips its second call of the music driver ($F8F8). 0 otherwise ($B4F4, $96AF).

How far the Vaus would pass a side wall (vaus_place $FCEE-$FD2B: left edge below $20, right edge above $DB); vaus_x is pulled back by it.

Colour (colour RAM AND 7) of the brick just broken ($B160); picks its points from the table $B2C4 ($B259).
Last value of frame_counter bit 3, so the current player's panel marker ($D8EF or $DA57) flashes every 8 frames ($FB8F-$FBB9).

16-bit scratch, high byte (with bits_lo).
Y saved over key_held ($0832/$085E).
Menu: the menu key (0-6) last seen held, so a held key acts once ($B5A9-$B5C9); $FF when none.

Brick hit: the brick row of the hit, from the ball's or the laser's Y ($AFAD-$B00C, $A6FF); +1 for the lower half ($B1C0); places the capsule ($B239) and picks the background pattern ($B2CD).
Brick hit: the screen column of the hit (even), from the ball's or the laser's X ($AFBB-$B00C, $A70E), stepped across the brick's cells ($B1A7, $B1D8).

Brick removal: $10 when a brick still stands on the shadow side of the cell (the cell above it, or above and to the left), so the background character put back is the shadowed one, else 0 ($B175-$B1A4).
Brick removal scratch: (row x 4) AND $0C, the row part of the background pattern ($B2D4).
Background fill ($F552): the pattern row offset, (row AND 3) x 4, added to bg_char_base for each screen row.

Row counter for screen builders: the background rows ($F582-$F5D8, to 25), the side walls ($F632-$F68A, to 24), the menu and story text lines ($B639-$B6E9), and save_wall_of_player's brick rows (1-16).

Wall builder: second byte of the row's brick-presence bits (bricks 8-12).

Frames (to $C0) before the next enemy is let in through a gate ($9F8A-$9F96).

Enemy collision scratch ($A232): the enemy's Y.
Fire button as last seen, so a press acts once (the menu $B5B2, the laser $A60B); copied from fire_now at each life ($9AD1), cleared by the menu ($B55F) and when the laser power starts ($A87C).
Fire button now (1 pressed), written by every input routine ($FCB8 paddles, $FCC4 others, $FE1D) and set to 1 in attract mode ($9568).

The falling capsule, 0 none, else its type 1-7: 1 S slow, 2 C catch, 3 E enlarge, 4 D disruption, 5 L laser, 6 B break, 7 P extra Vaus (handlers from $A858). Chosen when a brick breaks ($B223), cleared when it is caught or lost ($AA12).

Last frame_counter bit 2 seen by the capsule roll ($A7E1).

Ball speed, whole steps per frame less one: 2 at each life ($9ADB, 4 in attract mode), -1 by the S capsule (not below 1, $A8BA), +1 by the disruption ($A926), raised to frame_counter_hi / 4 as the round goes on, up to 11 ($ADE7). Break power: 1 when the B capsule is caught ($A86A); the next frame opens the exit in the right wall and makes it $FF ($A42C); the exit glyphs then animate. Cleared by the next capsule ($AA29).
Non-zero while the Vaus leaves through the open exit ($A477); stops the input ($FC99), the ball and most of the main loop ($9582).
1 when the Vaus is pushed against the right wall ($FD1F); with the exit open this starts the exit ($A46D). Cleared every frame the exit is closed ($A424).
Round 33: frames (0-4) between steps of Doh's mouth ($9819).
Round 33: position in Doh's mouth sequence $987E; a 0 entry fires shots from the free enemy slots ($984A).
Frame counter, high byte (+1 every 256 frames, $F73F); reset with the page each life. Raises the ball speed ($ADE7: ball_speed becomes this / 4) and steers the capsule choice ($B300).
Top-wall gate: 1 when open (stage 0 reached, $988F), 0 when shut ($9898); an enemy waits for it ($9FDA).

Top-wall gate: 1 while it opens or closes ($9FE1 for an enemy, $9FFB after it); cleared at the end ($988A, $9895).
Top-wall gate: stage 3 shut to 0 open, the glyphs at $CF58/$CF60 drawn from $9950/$9958 ($9928).
Read when an enemy enters ($9F9E: X $AF if non-zero, else $47; $9FCD: skip the gate wait). No instruction writes it; it is cleared with the page, so enemies always enter at X $47 through the gate.

Vaus explosion: 0 alive, else position+1 in the shape list $9C50 ($9B56); set when no ball is left ($9AF0). Pauses most of the main loop ($957F).
Ball steps left this frame (ball_speed + carry, at most 11, $ADCC).
Enemies, three slots ($024C-$024E): the characters above the enemy ORed ($A264); bit 7 set means a brick blocks the way up.
Enemies, three slots ($024F-$0251): bit 7 set when a brick is below ($A290).
Enemies, three slots ($0252-$0254): bit 7 set when a brick is to the right ($A2BB-$A2C8).
Enemies, three slots ($0255-$0257): bit 7 set when a brick is to the left ($A29F-$A2AC).

Enemies, three slots: frames since the last animation frame ($A361), against enemy_anim_delay.
Enemies, three slots: entry phase: 0 waiting for enemy_spawn_timer, 1 at the gate waiting for it to open ($9FC8), $80 coming down through it ($9FE9) until Y $38, then 0 with the enemy active ($A02C).

16 bytes ($0264-$0273), one colour code per brick of a row: unpacked from the round layout by the wall builder ($F437/$F43E), packed into the wall buffer by save_wall_of_player ($0691).
Enemies, three slots (objects 8-10, Y at $9435, X at $944D): 0 none, 1 moving ($9FFE), $FF exploding ($9F07). The intro uses the same slots for its attacker, shot and escaping Vaus.

Enemies, three slots: position in the frame list $A376 (a 0 ends a list, the byte after it says where to restart); set from $A3E8 by the round (AND 3, $9FB7, $F5F5), from $A3D8 for Doh's shots ($9865), 0 for the explosion ($9EFD).
enemy_anim of slot 1, set directly at the round's start ($F5F8).
enemy_anim of slot 2, set directly at the round's start ($F5FB).
Enemies, three slots: Y step, +1 down, $FF up, 0 still.
Enemies, three slots: X step, +1 right, $FF left, 0 still.
Enemies, three slots: $FF when Y is the axis that moves every step; otherwise the amount taken from enemy_acc per step, Y moving on a borrow ($A2DB-$A30C, set by $B3FA).
Enemies, three slots: the amount taken from enemy_acc per step when Y is the major axis, X moving on a borrow.

Enemies, three slots: added back to enemy_acc on a borrow (the larger distance, $B453).
Enemies, three slots: Y direction to resume after an obstacle ($A105, $A1B6).
Enemies, three slots: X direction to resume after an obstacle ($A027, $A0B1).
Enemies, three slots: frames per animation frame ($A3F0 by round AND 3 at $9FC3, 1 for the explosion $9F02, 2 for Doh's shots $986F).

Balls, three slots: frames (5 after the Vaus, 2 after the top wall) before the ball may bounce off the Vaus again ($AC6D, $B3D0, $ACCC).

Per-frame filter program (first of the seven calls at $F892). Off while mode $24D0 = 0. Cutoff runs in $24D3/$24D4: during the delay $24CF it waits, or with mode bit 1 adds the fourth delta each frame; then four phases, each adding its 16-bit delta ($24C3/$24C5/$24C7/$24C9) once per frame for its count ($24D5-$24D8). When all four are spent: mode bit 7 restarts from the start cutoff (filter_restart), bit 0 repeats from the current one (filter_reload), neither holds. Writes $D415 = cutoff AND 7 and $D416 = cutoff / 8 (an 11-bit cutoff)

Voice 0 sequencer, once per sound tick: does nothing unless $2545 is set; counts down the note length $E6 and at 0 reads events from ($E0): command bytes $C0-$F0 (even) dispatch through the vector table $3F00 until a note or rest is read. Events are two bytes, a note byte b ($00-$BF) and a length: the note number is b, or b - $60 when b >= $60; note $5F is a rest (the sound goes on, nothing restarts); the length is entry $2549 + second byte of the note-length table when b < $60, or the second byte itself, in ticks, when b >= $60

Voice 0 effects, once per sound tick, for music and sound effects alike; nothing while the life counter $24F5 is 0. Gate: with the control flag bit 3, the gate drops when the remaining length $E6 falls below the gate time $24F4; otherwise $24F4 counts down and the gate drops at 0 ($FF holds). After the gate drops, life $24F5 counts down ($FF never) and at 0 voice 0's registers $D400-$D406 are cleared and, if voice 0 is the filter voice, the filter program is stopped ($24D0 = 0). Pulse program (mode $24EA): after the delay $24E9, the width $F1/$F2 adds delta 1 ($24EB) for $24FA ticks, then delta 2 ($24ED) for $24FB ticks; at the end mode bit 7 restarts from the start width, bit 0 repeats, neither holds; written to $D402/$D403. Pitch program (mode $24E6): after the delay $24E5 (or, with mode bit 1, sliding by delta 4 during it), the frequency $F7/$F8 adds deltas 1-4 ($24D9-$24E0) for counts $24F6-$24F9; at the end bit 7 restarts at the note's pitch, bit 0 repeats; written to $D400/$D401

Start of the self-erasing protection area $5F40-$5F86, which the loop at $5F86 fills with $01 when the check passes, so after start-up every byte here reads $01. These two bytes ($44 $45, an undocumented NOP $45) never run: the routine is entered at $5F42 from $B9DE

Copy protection, called once from the start-up at $B9DE. Writes 1 to CIA 1 timer A low ($DC04), control $D9 to $DC0E, calls $A949 (decrypts $BA0A-$BA6A by XOR with $A71A-$A77A), then writes A to the serial data register $DC0C and loops: restart the timer ($DC0E = $D9), wait for the timer A bit (bit 0) in $DC0D, keep the whole interrupt register in $BA65, and start again unless the serial-port bit (bit 3) is also set. On a machine whose serial port never completes, this hangs. Then it waits three more timer underflows ($5F72), writes $DC0C again, and overwrites $5F40-$5F86 (itself, up to the STA $DC0C) with $01 (A = 1 from the AND #$01). Returns with X = $FF. Undocumented NOPs at $5F44 and $5F4E pad it to mislead a disassembler
$44 $6D: the undocumented NOP $6D (zero page), two bytes that do nothing; the disassembler cannot decode it. Part of the protection routine $5F42, before STA $DC04.
protection_serial_check, continued after the undocumented NOP at $5F44: STA $DC04 (timer A low = 1), LDA #$D9 / STA $DC0E (start timer A, serial port as output)

$1C $AD $08: the undocumented NOP $08AD,X, three bytes that read memory and do nothing; it hides the JSR $A949 that follows from a decoder that knows only the documented set. Part of the protection routine $5F42.
protection_serial_check, continued after the undocumented NOP at $5F4E: JSR $A949 (decrypt $BA0A-$BA6A), then STA $DC0C sends a byte out of CIA 1's serial port; the wait loop at $5F57 follows
serial-port wait loop: restart timer A, poll $DC0D, store it in $BA65 (read back by $5F66 and later code)
self-erase: X = $46 down to 0 stores A ($01) at $5F40-$5F86; the loop itself ($5F88-$5F8E) survives

For every live ball (2..0, $02A7) and live enemy (2..0, $0274 = 1): ball_enemy_v ($9E30) and ball_enemy_h ($9E96). A hit destroys the enemy and bounces the ball.

Ball X against enemy Y, vertical: if the ball moving up ($0295 < 0) / down is within a 24 x 24 box ($0C each way) of the enemy, destroy it (enemy_destroyed) and, if the ball's bat cooldown $02AA is 0, set the ball's vertical direction to down (+1) / up ($FF).

Ball X against enemy Y, by the ball's horizontal direction ($0298): moving right, enemy X within (ball X - 12, ball X + 12] and Y within 12 -> enemy_destroyed and $0298 = $FF if the bat cooldown $02AA,X is 0. Moving left the test can never pass: after SBC #$0C the code does SBC #$18 (should be ADC), so it needs enemy X > ball X - 12 and <= ball X - 37 at once ($9E9B-$9EAB); the vertical test still catches such balls.

Enemy (or Doh's shot) in slot Y destroyed: explosion animation from index 0 of anim_lists, speed 1, $0274,Y = $FF (dying), colour yellow ($F821,Y = 7); effect sound on three voices unless a priority-2 sound runs ($0216/$0217); add BCD $10 to the score's low byte ($0933, via $FBBD; the capsule adds $01 to the next byte). Returns A = $02AA,X, the bat cooldown of ball X, which the ball tests use to decide the bounce.

Enemies, three slots, on 161 frames in 256 ($021F += $A1, carry). Live slot ($0274 = 1): enemy_probe $A22F, enemy_steer_v $A182, enemy_steer $A051, move_object $A2DB, animate_object $A344. Dying ($FF): animate only. Idle (0): count $0229 to $C0 (192 updates), then put an enemy at Y $1E, X $47 with animation/colour/speed by round index AND 3 (enemy_anim_start, enemy_colour, enemy_anim_speed) and $025E = 1; wait for the gate (update_gate: open it if closed), then $025E = $80: move down 1 per update to Y $38, where the enemy goes live heading down, horizontal preference toward the Vaus ($028F), and the gate closes.
Drum sequencer return stack: push $DA/$DB + A (the address after the current command) at $78,X/$80,X with X = $DD, then $DD - 1. Used by drum_call ($A449) and drum_repeat ($A7C9).

Steer a live enemy X. At Y = $B8 aim it once at the Vaus ($A043: $B3FA, flag $0258); below $B8 keep the course (flag cleared). Higher up, only on frames where $0201 is 0, $40, $80 or $C0 or below $10, re-plan from the cells around it ($024C up, $024F down, $0252 right, $0255 left; negative = brick): with no vertical step head down if free ($A0F6); with no sideways step pick one: left when the Vaus's $9445 is at or right of the enemy, else right, unless a brick is that side; otherwise reverse the vertical or horizontal step where a brick allows. Writes $027A/$027D, $0280/$0283, $028C/$028F.
Enemy with no vertical step: if the cell below is free ($024F >= 0), head down ($027A = 1) with $0280 = $80 and remember $028C = 1.

Enemy X blocked: if its vertical step points at a brick ($024C above / $024F below negative), or it moves only sideways and its horizontal step does ($0252 / $0255), turn: from vertical to sideways in the remembered direction $028F (or the other way if that side is blocked, $A1A9-$A21D), from sideways to down or up ($A115-$A17F), keeping the old step in $028C/$028F; with both ways blocked reverse ($A220, $A109).
Drum bytecode $60 (return): pop the return address: $DD + 1, $DA/$DB = $78,X/$80,X (the entry at $A1EA is also used by drum_next to reload without popping).
Load $DA/$DB from the return-stack entry X ($78,X / $80,X) without popping; drum_next uses it to jump back to the start of a repeat.

Read the screen around enemy X into $024C (cell above: row (Y-$31)/8, columns (X-$14)/8 and +1, ORed), $024F (two rows lower, the cell below), $0255 (left: column (X-$15)/8, two rows ORed) and $0252 (right: column (X-4)/8); a character $80 or above (a brick or wall) makes the value negative. Rows come from the screen-row table $F78B. Nothing above Y $31. Then, if $0944 is non-zero, JSR wipe_memory ($A523).
This byte is the operand of LDA $944D,X; the drum sequencer at $FF33 reads $A253,X with X = $80-$87 as the high byte of each sample handler, so the table it uses is drum_handler_hi at $A2D3-$A2DA.

High bytes of the drum sample handlers for bytecodes $81-$87 (low bytes at $B0FE-$B104): $81 $F604, $82 $F345, $83 $AEEF, $84 $B500, $85 $B290, $86 $ACD6, $87 $F62F. The entry for $80, $A2D3, is the RTS of enemy_probe ($60), so $80 would call $60B0; no track found uses $80.

Move object slot X (enemies, Doh's shots, the intro's sprites) one step by Bresenham: if $0280,X = $FF, Y += $027A every step and X += $027D when $0286 - $0283 borrows (reload + $0289); otherwise X moves every step and Y when $0286 - $0280 borrows. Y $F2 or more (off the bottom) removes the object (move_object_off: $0274, Y and X = 0).
Remove object slot X: $0274,X = 0 (idle), obj_y and obj_x of the slot = 0.

Animate object slot X: when the counter $025B,X passes the speed $0292,X (every speed + 1 calls) show the next sprite pointer from anim_lists at index $0277,X into $F82D,X; a 0 in the list is followed by the index to loop to, or by a second 0 = end, which removes the object (object_off).

Sprite pointer lists for animate_object, each ended by 0 and a loop index: at 0 the explosion $7B-$83 then 0 0 (end, object removed); $0B enemy type 1, $4A-$51; $15 type 2, $52-$5E; $24 type 3, $6D-$72; $2C type 4, 40 frames of $9A-$A7 and $5F; $56 Doh's shot $60-$6A; $65 the same frames reversed. The bytes at $A3D8-$A3DA and $A3E8-$A3F3 inside it double as tables.
Start index for Doh's shot in slot 0-2: $56, $65, $56 (read at $9862). The first byte is also the loop index of the list at $56 in anim_lists.
Enemy animation start by round index AND 3: $0B, $15, $24, $2C (rounds 1, 5, 9 ... use type 1 and so on); read at $9FB4 and by $F5F2.
Enemy sprite colour by round index AND 3: 6, 6, 6, 6 (blue), into $F821,X at $9FBD.
Enemy animation speed (frames per sprite, $0292,X) by round index AND 3: 3, 2, 4, 3.

The Vaus materialises at the start of a round or life: every 4th frame (bit 2 of $0201) set its pointer pair ($F825/$F826) from vaus_appear_frames backwards: $79, $77, $75, $73, then $40 (the normal Vaus) and stop.
Left-half sprite pointers for vaus_appear, read from the end: 0 (stop), $40, $73, $75, $77, $79.

The B (break) capsule's exit. $023C = 0: clear $023E and return. $023C = 1 (just caught): $023C = $FF, open the exit in the right wall (characters at $CF40-$CF57 from $CF68, colour 9 at screen rows 22-24 column 27). $023C = $FF: scroll the exit's 24 bitmap bytes by one each frame; when the Vaus touches it ($023E, set at $FD1F) start leaving ($023D = 1, $0247 = $17, width 4, sound), slide both halves right 1 pixel a frame to X $E0, then set the bits of the sprite data at $E5C0, then $E580, one pixel column per frame (round_start restores it from $E600); when done and the tune is over, JMP round_cleared. No score is added on this path.
Drum bytecode $20 lo hi (call): push the address after it (drum_push with A = 3), then fall into drum_jump.
Drum bytecode $4C lo hi (jump): $DA/$DB = the inline address. Also the second half of drum_call.

Called from enemy_probe only when $0944 is non-zero, which no code found sets (it is 0 at the hand-over and in play; in the stale build at $94D8 $0944 was the attract counter). Copies the 33 bytes at $A53A-$A55A to $01C0 with undocumented NOPs between the instructions, SEI and JMP $01C0. Not executed in the simulator.
Undocumented opcodes, shown as bytes: $A525 NOP $45; $A527 LDA $A53A,Y; $A52A NOP $45; $A52C STA $01C0,Y; $A52F NOP $45; $A531 DEY; $A532 BPL $A525; $A534 NOP $A9; $A536 SEI; $A537 JMP $01C0.

Code copied to $01C0 by wipe_memory and run there: LDA $0E / SBC #$BE / STA $0E / LDA #$FA / LDA #$9D / then copy page after page from ($11),Y to ($0D),Y until $0E wraps / LDX #0 / PHA / DEX / BNE: overwrites memory and the stack, a deliberate crash. The copy takes 33 bytes, so its last 6 are the drum data at $A555.

Drum bytecode figures called by drums_title: $A555 (8 x $83 1+3, 8 x $85 1+3, then $86 2+14 x 4), $A56F ($86 2+14), $A574 (a 12-call bar), $A598 ($82 1, 1, 6), $A59F, $A5A5 ($86 2+6), $A5AA, $A5B0 ($81 2+6), $A5B5 and $A5BB (with $84). Waits are in sequencer ticks. Decoded: work/agent12/drums.txt.

Turn the Vaus into its laser shape: every 2nd frame (bit 1 of $0201) set the pointer pair $F825/$F826 from laser_on_frames[$0223] and count $0223 down: $73 $75 $77 $79 $77 $75 $73 then $43 (the laser Vaus). Returns Y = $0223.
Left-half pointers for laser_on_shape, read from the end: 0, $43, $73, $75, $77, $79, $77, $75, $73.

The laser (L). If $022B is set and the Vaus has normal width ($020A = 4): run laser_on_shape; once it has finished, fire (fire_laser) each time the fire button $0236 goes from pressed to released ($0235 keeps the last state). Then for each live shot (1..0, $022C): if spent ($0230) step its burst ($F827 + 1 every 2nd frame up to $49, then remove); else move it up 4, and when it gets above Y $3A mark it spent; test bricks (laser_vs_bricks) and enemies (laser_vs_enemies).
Laser shot X against the live enemies: Y within $0C-$10 above the enemy and X within $0C either side -> enemy_destroyed and the shot is spent ($0230 = 1).
Test the laser shot's two beams, at X - $1A and X - $0B ($0211), against the brick cell under the shot (laser_beam_brick).

One beam of a laser shot: nothing at Y $C0 or more; above Y $3B the shot is removed ($A666). Else read the screen cell at row (Y-$3B)/8 + 1, column 2*((X - $0211)/16) + 1 (via the row table $F78B); a character $80 or above is a brick: put its cell in $0218/$0219 (row (Y-$33)/8, column ((X-$0211)/8) AND $FE), break it ($B108) and mark the shot spent ($0230).

Live enemies (or Doh's shots) touching the Vaus: enemy Y within (Vaus Y - 8, Vaus Y + $1A] and X within (centre - 2*width, centre + width + 3] ($0206, $020A). In rounds 1-32 the enemy is destroyed (enemy_destroyed); in round 33 the shot destroys the Vaus (JMP vaus_destroyed). Its own 97 bytes, $A71A-$A77A, are the XOR key with which $A949 decrypts $BA0A-$BA6A at start-up, so changing this code changes what that decryption produces.

Fire a laser shot: the first idle shot slot (1, then 0, $022C) gets X = Vaus centre - 4, Y $E8, pointer $45, colour white; then an effect sound on three voices unless a priority-2 sound runs. One slot per press.
Drum bytecode $49 n (repeat n times): push the address after it (A = 2), store n in $89,X (the count slot of the new entry), continue after it. The matching $40 is drum_next.

Roll the capsule's letter: every 4th frame (bit 2 of $0201, kept in $0239) step $0238 (7..0) and rebuild the 10 rows of the capsule sprite at $E541 (every 3rd byte) from its base $E501 masked by capsule_mask and ORed with the 8-byte letter capsule_letter_now, both indexed by ($0238 + row) AND 7, so the letter scrolls through the capsule.
The falling capsule's letter, 8 bytes, copied here from capsule_letters by $B22C when the capsule appears; zeros at the hand-over.

Capsule letters, 8 bytes each (3 blank rows, 5 rows of a 4-pixel multicolour letter, pixel pairs 01 on 10), for types 1-7 at $A818 + 8(type-1); $B22C copies type x 8 - 7 .. type x 8 from $A817: S $A818, C $A820, E $A828, D $A830, L $A838, B $A840, P $A848. The first byte, $A817, is the end of type 0's empty cell.
Mask for capsule_letter: $FF $FF $FF then five $00, so the three rows that are blank in each letter keep the capsule's base graphic and the five letter rows are replaced.
Capsule effects by type ($0237), words for the self-modified JSR at $A9FA: 0 none, 1 S $A8BA, 2 C $A8AC, 3 E $AA44, 4 D $A8CD, 5 L $A870, 6 B $A868, 7 P $A882. Letters from capsule_letters.
High bytes of capsule_actions (second byte of each word), read at $A9F4 into $A9FC.
B: arm the break exit ($023C = 1, break_exit opens it) and clear the capsule.
L: laser on ($022B = 1), start the shape change ($0223 = 8) and clear the remembered fire state ($0235 = 0); clear the capsule.
P: one more life for the current player (BCD $0936,X + 1, not stored when it would pass 99), redraw the panel ($FA4E, $F39B), priority sound ($0216 = $28, $0217 = 2), tune $2F; clear the capsule.
C: catch on ($022A = 1): the next time the ball meets the Vaus it is held (bat_collision); clear the capsule.
INC $D020 / JMP $A8B4: an endless border-colour loop with no caller found, between two capsule actions; looks like a leftover debugging trap.
S: ball speed $023A - 1 unless that would be 0, and clear the fraction $0248. The speed floor in move_balls ($ADE7, frames since the life began / 1024) can raise it again on the next frame.

D: split the ball into three: copy the first live ball's (2, 1, else 0) X, Y and vertical direction to all three slots, live, horizontal directions from disrupt_dx (+1, -1, +1) and angles $029B = $FF, $029E from disrupt_angle ($40, $F0, $FF); then ball speed $023A + 1. The loop also writes 0 to $0228,X for X = 0-2, which clears $0229 (enemy timer) and $022A (catch) as well as the held flag.
Horizontal directions of balls 0-2 after the D capsule: +1, -1, +1.
$029E (the second Bresenham ratio) of balls 0-2 after the D capsule: $40, $F0, $FF.
Drum bytecode $40 (end of repeat): count down $88,X of the top entry; not zero -> reload $DA/$DB from it (back to the start); zero -> drop it and step past the $40.
Start-up, called from the protection at $5F51: XOR the 97 bytes $BA0A-$BA6A with $A71A-$A77A (the code of vaus_vs_enemies and the start of fire_laser), Y = $60 down to 0.

Code with no caller found and never executed in the simulator: for each hard brick ($0456 down to 1) with a shine flag, set it to $80, add 1 to $0355,X if not negative, and redraw its two characters ($8D/$91 gold or $85/$89 silver from $03AA,X). Similar to silver_shine; possibly left from an earlier build. Its BEQ goes to $A948, an RTS.

The falling capsule ($0237 = type, 0 none): roll its letter, and if it overlaps the Vaus (Y within Vaus Y + 4 .. + $0C, X within centre - 2*width .. + width + $0C) and the Vaus is not leaving: add $01 to the score's middle byte ($0934, via $FBBD), cancel the running powers ($AA17), remember the type in $0208 and call its action through capsule_actions (self-modified JSR at $A9FA). Otherwise it falls 1 pixel a frame and disappears at Y $FA.
JSR to the capsule action: its operand ($A9FB/$A9FC) is written from capsule_actions just before; as assembled it points at itself.
Low byte of the self-modified JSR at $A9FA, written at $A9F1.
High byte of the self-modified JSR at $A9FA, written at $A9F7.
No capsule: capsule_y = 0, type $0237 = 0. Every capsule action ends here.

On catching a capsule: if the laser was on, start the shape back ($0223 = 8); catch, laser and break off ($022A, $022B, $023C = 0); release a held ball (ball_release); $F6C2; if the Vaus is enlarged ($020A = $0C) start shrinking it ($0207 = $80).
E: start enlarging the Vaus ($0207 = 1, grown by vaus_resize), priority sound ($0216 = $28, $0217 = 2) on three voices; clear the capsule.

While a ball is held ($0228): release it (ball_release) when fire is pressed ($0236) or the frame counter $0201 reaches $80; otherwise keep the first live ball (2, 1, else 0) on the Vaus at X = $0206 - $0221 (the offset where it was caught), Y = Vaus Y + 8.

More drum bytecode called by drums_title: $AAA0 (a bar of seven calls), $AAB5 and $AACF (bars with sample $83 on the off-beats), each ending in a jump to $A5A5 or $A574. Decoded: work/agent12/drums.txt.
Release the held ball: ball 0's bat cooldown $02AA = 5, $0228 = 0, launch sound on three voices ($272F).
Drum track of the ending (start_drums from $968C): sample $87, then repeats of $85, $82, $83, $84 and four bars built from drum_bar ($98F9), looping from $AB12. Decoded: work/agent12/drums.txt.

Every 4th frame ($0225): step the shine of each hard brick (silver or gold, $0456 down to 1) whose flag $0300,X is $80: both characters at its screen address ($03AA,X) go down by one (left) / left + 4 (right); when the right one reaches $86 (silver) or $8E (gold) the shine is over: flag = 1 and $0355,X - 1 unless negative (gold has $80). The shine starts at $B044 when such a brick is hit, and for every hard brick at the start of a round ($F4F1), whose count is therefore decremented once then.

Balls against the Vaus (bat), once per ball step from move_balls; nothing while a ball is held. Hit when ball Y is Vaus Y + $0A..$0C and ball X within centre - 2*width .. centre + width + $13 ($0206, $020A). With the bat cooldown $02AA,X at 0: d = centre + 6 - ball X, halved when the Vaus is enlarged. Left side (d >= 0): ball goes left; d < 4 angle $FF/$F0, 4-7 $FF/$40, 8+ $80/$FF ($029B/$029E). Right side ($AD02, |d|): ball goes right; |d| < 4 $FF/$40, 4-7 $FF/$F0, 8+ $80/$FF, so the two inner zones are swapped between the sides. Reverse the vertical direction, offset $0221 = centre - ball X, cooldown 5. With catch on ($022A) and no priority sound: hold the ball ($0228 = 1, $0201 = 1) with its sound; else the bounce sound.

Drum sample $86: 6 x 20 steps; each waits a delay from $FD75,Y and writes the low nibble of a running sum ($DE += $98) to the volume register (STA $D418 made by adding $40 to the operand's high byte at $ACF5, restored to $9418 at the end).
High byte of the STA at $ACF3: $94 as assembled (STA $9418, harmless), $D4 while drum_sample_86 runs (STA $D418).
Enlarge or shrink the Vaus: $0207 positive: width $020A + 1 a frame up to $0C (not while the laser shape changes, $0223); $0207 negative: width - 1 down to 4. $0207 = 0 when done.
While $0223 is non-zero: every 2nd frame set the Vaus pointers from laser_off_frames[$0223] and count down: $73 $75 $77 $79 $77 $75 $73 then $40, the normal Vaus.
Left-half pointers for laser_off_shape, read from the end: 0, $40, $73, $75, $77, $79, $77, $75, $73.

The balls' movement, unless one is held ($0228). Steps this frame = speed $023A + carry of the fraction ($0248 += $023B), at most $0B; for each step move every live ball one step ($B334), test it against bricks (ball_vs_bricks), then all against the Vaus (bat_collision). Then the speed floor: if $0241 / 4 (frames since the life began / 1024) is above $023A and below $0C, $023A takes it and the fraction $023B restarts.

Ball X against the bricks, for Y $3B-$BF: by its directions look at the cell ahead vertically (row from (Y-$3B)/8 moving up, (Y-$38)/8 moving down; column 2*((X-$1E)/16) + 1) and horizontally ((X-$18)/8 moving left, (X-$24)/8 + 2 moving right); a character $80 or more is a brick or wall. On a hit: reverse that direction, count the bounce ($02AD,X; at 50 bounce_reangle), put the cell in $0218/$0219 (cell_above / cell_below / cell_left / cell_right), break it ($B108) and add to the speed fraction (speed_up).
Brick to the left: reverse the horizontal direction, count, cell_left, $B108, speed_up.
Brick to the right: reverse the horizontal direction, count, cell_right, $B108, speed_up.

Drum sample $83: 6 x 25 steps; each waits a delay from $F7E5,Y and writes the low nibble of $DE += $65 to the volume register through the STA at $AF0C, whose high byte $AF0E is $D4 during the sample and $94 otherwise.
High byte of the STA at $AF0C: assembled as $D4 (STA $D418), set to $D4 at $AEF6 and back to $94 (STA $9418) at $AF17.
Brick below: reverse the vertical direction, count, cell_below, $B108, speed_up.
Brick above: reverse the vertical direction, count, cell_above, speed_up, $B108.
Each brick hit: the ball-speed fraction $023B + 4, held at $FC (no store on overflow).

Change ball X's angle when its brick-bounce count $02AD,X reaches 50 (ball_vs_bricks; also called from $B3F6): from $FF/x to $80/$FF, otherwise to $FF/$F0 or $FF/$40 by the low bit of the raster line ($D012); count = 0. Keeps a ball from repeating one path for ever.
Cell of the brick above ball X for $B108: $0218 = (Y - $33)/8, $0219 = ((X - $1E)/8) AND $FE.
Cell of the brick below ball X: $0218 = (Y - $2E)/8, $0219 = ((X - $1E)/8) AND $FE.
Cell of the brick to the left of ball X: $0218 = (Y - $33)/8, $0219 = ((X - $21)/8) AND $FE.
Cell of the brick to the right of ball X: $0218 = (Y - $33)/8, $0219 from X (continues at $B000).

A ball has hit a gold brick (from brick_hit via the JMP at $B105; not reached in the simulator's round 1). Adds Y to the screen pointer ($0D), finds the special brick with that screen address in $03AA/$03AB (entries $0456 down to 1), redraws it as $8D $91, sets its flag $0300 = $80 and, unless $0216 is set, starts a sound on three voices ($272F with $2174, $2193, $21B2). Gold bricks are never removed.

A ball has hit a silver brick (from brick_hit via $B0FB). Finds the special brick at the hit screen address as gold_brick_hit does; if its hit counter $0355 is zero (counted down at $ABA6) the entry is cleared, the pointer put back and the brick is destroyed like a normal one ($B16D); otherwise it is redrawn as $85 $89, flagged $80 and, unless $0216 is set, the same three-voice sound starts.

Not a table of its own: $B07D is the base that drum_script_step adds the drum number ($80-$87) to at $FF2D, so the drum routines' low bytes are $B0FD-$B104. $B0FD is the high byte of the JMP at $B0FB ($B0), which would give drum $80 the address $60B0 in the title picture's colours; whether the script ever plays drum $80 was not checked.

Low bytes of the title percussion routines for drums $81-$87: $04 $45 $EF $00 $90 $D6 $2F; with the high bytes at $A2D4-$A2DA: $F604 (drum_81), $F345 (drum_82), $AEEF, $B500 (drum_84), $B290 (drum_85), $ACD6, and $F62F, an RTS (a rest).
brick_hit's way to gold_brick_hit (JMP $B010), placed here, after drum_lo_81_87, within reach of the branch at $B167.

A ball or shot has hit the playfield cell at ($0D),Y (colour at ($0F),Y; X = the ball). Called from $A711, $AEC6, $AEE8, $AF36, $AF5B. On round 33 (round index $20) a screen code from $80 to $E7 is a hit on Doh: $0455 - 1, $0215 = 1 and a three-voice sound. Otherwise aligns Y to the brick's first cell, clears the ball's step accumulator $02A1,X, keeps the brick's colour (AND 7) in $020E, and sends gold (code $8A or more) to gold_brick_hit and silver ($82 or more) to silver_brick_hit. A normal brick: $0455 - 1; both cells and the shaded cells below-right get the background back (background_char_at, with the shaded variant $10 higher where a brick still casts its shadow). Then a capsule, when none is falling ($0237 = 0), exactly one ball is in play ($02A7-$02A9 sum to 1) and bricks remain: type from choose_capsule (1-7, never the same as the last, $0208, which is skipped to the next), colour from capsule_colours into slot 7, $0237 = type, 8 bytes from $A810 + 8 x type to $A80F, slot 7 placed at the brick (Y = row x 8 + $32 in $9434, X in $944C). Finally points: brick_points by colour into $0933, the ball's wall-bounce count $02AD,X = 0, a sound unless $0216 is set, and add_score.

Title-tune percussion sound $85, reached only through the JSR at $FEE8. Patches its store at $B2AD to STA $D418, then 6 x 25 steps, each a delay of drum_85_delays+Y ($F959) counts and the low nibble of $DE (advanced by $DD) as the SID volume; restores STA $9418. Holds the CPU while it plays.
Operand high byte of drum_85's volume store at $B2AD: $D4 in the image as loaded (the store live), $94 (STA $9418, harmless) once drum_85 has run, $D4 while it plays.
Sprite colour of each capsule type 1-7 (entry 0 unused): $08 $05 $06 $03 $02 $0A $0B, put into slot 7's colour ($F820) by brick_hit.

Points for a normal brick by its colour (colour RAM AND 7, entries 0-7): $00 $10 $08 $12 $09 $11 $07 $13, BCD into $0933; the panel's fixed last 0 makes them 100, 80, 120, 90, 110, 70 and 130 for colours 1-7.

Returns in A the background screen code for the cell at row $0218, column $0219: $0458 + (row x 4 AND $0C) + (column AND 3), the playfield's 4 x 4 tile (draw_playfield_background). Used by brick_hit to repaint a broken brick's cells.

Chooses the capsule for a broken brick from the frame counter $0201: $A0-$FF and $0A-$1F give $FF (none). $20-$9F: (frame XOR the ball's X) AND 3 gives 2, 2, 1, 2. $00-$09: 6 if bit 1 of the current player's lives (BCD) is set; else 5 if $0241 (frames / 256) is $12 or more; else 4 if the round has 4 or more special bricks ($0456); else 3 if the ball's Y is below $80, otherwise as for $20-$9F. Called from brick_hit.

Moves ball X (0-2, virtual sprite 4 + X: Y $9431,X, X $9449,X) one step along its line. If $029B,X = $FF, Y changes every call by $0295,X and X by $0298,X when the accumulator $02A1,X (less $029E,X, modulus $02A4,X) borrows; otherwise the accumulator takes $029B,X, Y moves on a borrow and X every call. Y below $3B: bounces down ($0295 negated, Y + 1, $02AA,X = 2). Y of $FC or more: the ball is lost ($02A7,X = 0, its Y and X cleared). X below $24 moving left, or $E8 or more moving right: bounces off the side wall ($0298 negated, X nudged back, accumulator cleared) and counts $02AD,X; at 50 such bounces without a brick, JSR $AF6B. Called from $ADD6.

Sets up a straight path from virtual sprite 8 + X (X $944D,X, Y $9435,X) to the Vaus's position ($9445, $942D): directions $027D,X (X: 1 right, $FF left) and $027A,X (Y: 1 down, $FF up), and for the longer axis $FF in $0283,X or $0280,X with the distances in $0286/$0289 and the other of $0280/$0283. Called from the intro animation ($0725, $0765, $07AE, $07D5) and $9872, $A048.
Waits for the next tick: loops until $0200 (counted up once a frame by nmi_frame_a) is non-zero, then takes one off. The game's frame pacing: the main loop and the menus call it once per pass.
High bytes of the title percussion script's command handlers ($A4 $A9 $A1 $A7 $A4), with drum_command_lo at $F8A8: $A449, $A932, $A1E6, $A7C9, $A44E for commands $20, $40, $60, $49, $4C.

Shows the title picture: $D011 = $2B (bitmap, display off), video bank 1 ($DD00 = $C2), $D018 = $80 (bitmap $4000, colours $6000), border 0, background 1, the 1024 bytes at $6400-$67FF into colour RAM, the 12 virtual sprites' Y set to the last byte copied ($0B, from $6701), then $D011 = $3B (bitmap, display on). Called from title_screen, main_entry and $968F.

The title: picture (show_title_picture), sound silenced, percussion script reset (drum_script_init), $0209 = $FF (the NMI steps the script), tune $3D, $9945 (A = 2, X = $60, Y = $99), then title_wait_loop. Called from main_entry ($F023).

Plays the percussion (drum_play) until a key in keyboard row 7 or any joystick line in either port is active ($DC01 AND $DC00 differs from $7F): then $0209 = 0 and returns. If the tune ends first ($3417 zero), $0209 = 0 and JMP $9500, the attract mode. Also called from $9692.

Title-tune percussion sound $84, reached only through the JSR at $FEE8. Patches its store at $B51D to STA $D418, then 6 x 25 steps, each a delay of drum_84_delays+Y ($FCE8) counts and the low nibble of $DE (advanced by $DD) as the SID volume; restores STA $9418. Holds the CPU while it plays.
Operand high byte of drum_84's volume store at $B51D: $D4 while it plays, $94 (STA $9418, harmless) otherwise.
Resets the title percussion: no drum due ($DF = 0), wait $DC = $FF, script pointer ($DA) = $9A71.

Switches to the screen used by the menu, story and play: video bank 3 ($DD00 = $90), screen $C000 and character set $C800 ($D018 = $02), text mode on ($D011 = $1B), colours $D020-$D026 from play_screen_colours.

The input menu, then the story. Clears the screen, prints the menu, clears fire ($0235, $0236), sprites off, players $0939 from the remembered $093A; unless the device is the mouse, waits until $DC01 reads $FF (port 1 and keyboard row 7 released). Then once a tick: menu keys (menu_keys) and the menu redrawn (draw_menu_choices) until menu_keys reports fire released after a press. Then clears the screen, prints the story, waits 250 ticks and turns all sprites on.

Polls the menu keys (menu_key_codes, through key_held $0832): a key different from the last ($0214) chooses the device (N J K P: $093F = 0-3), the players (1, 2: $0939 = $093A = 0 or 1) or toggles one/two devices (D: $0940), returning Z set. With no key, reads the device (read_input_move_vaus) and returns Z clear only when the fire state $0236 has changed to 0: the game starts as fire is released.
Key numbers (8 x row + column) of the menu keys, in the order of their meaning: $27 N, $22 J, $25 K, $29 P, $38 1, $3B 2, $12 D.

menu_keys, after a key was found (Y = its index in menu_key_codes): ignored if it is the key already held ($0214, then the fire check); Y 0-3 sets the device $093F; Y 4-5 sets the players $0939 and $093A to 0 or 1; Y 6 (D) flips one/two devices $0940. Returns A = 0 (Z set: stay in the menu).
Low bytes of the screen addresses of the four device lines' markers: $5A $AA $FA $4A (with menu_marker_hi: $C05A, $C0AA, $C0FA, $C14A, rows 2, 4, 6 and 8, column 10).
High bytes of the device markers' screen addresses: $C0 $C0 $C0 $C1.

Shows the menu's choices: blanks the four device markers and puts $C7 beside the chosen device ($093F); writes the players digit '1' + $0939 at $C1EE (row 12) and the devices digit '1' + $0940 at $C19E (row 10), making 1 PLAYER / 2 PLAYER and 1 DEVICE / 2 DEVICE.

Prints menu_text from row 0. The format, shared by print_story_text and print_ending_text: a column byte, PETSCII capitals (a space becomes $1C, everything else AND $3F gives the screen code), $00 ends the line and moves two rows down, a byte with bit 7 set ($FF) ends the text. Rows come from screen_row_addresses.
Prints story_text from row 4 (format as print_menu_text). Called from input_menu.
Prints ending_text from row 4 (format as print_menu_text). Called from $969F after Doh; not reached in the simulator.
Clears the text screen: $1C (blank) into $C000-$C3E7 and colour 3 into $D800-$DBE7 (STA $BFFF,Y and the like with Y = $FA down to 1).

The input menu's text (print_menu_text format): SELECT YOUR INPUT DEVICE / NEOS MOUSE / JOYSTICK / KEYBOARD / PADDLES / 1 DEVICE / 1 PLAYER / SELECT OPTION USING FIRST LETTER / N J K P D 1 2 PLAYERS / FIRE BUTTON STARTS GAME / DISCONNECT MOUSE TO SELECT OPTION / @ TAITO 1986 @ IMAGINE 1984 (@ is screen code 0).

The story before round 1 (print_story_text): THE ERA AND TIME OF THIS STORY / IS UNKNOWN / AFTER THE MOTHERSHIP  ARKANOID / WAS DESTROYED A SPACECRAFT VAUS / SCRAMBLED AWAY FROM IT / BUT ONLY TO BE TRAPPED IN SPACE / BY SOMEONE.

The ending after Doh (print_ending_text): DIMENSION CONTROLLING FORT DOH / HAS NOW BEEN DEMOLISHED AND TIME / STARTED FLOWING BACKWARDS VAUS / MANAGED TO ESCAPE FROM THE DISTORTED / SPACE BUT THE REAL VOYAGE OF ARKANOID / IN THE GALAXY HAS ONLY NOW STARTED.

Every other frame ($0201 bit 0 clear) puts the next shape from title_sprite_frames ($0243 counts) into virtual sprite 8's shape ($F82D), stopping at the list's 0. Called once a tick by main_entry's loop while the tune plays.
Shapes for title_sprite_animate: $D1 $D2 $D3 $D4 $D3 $D2 $D1 $D5, then 0 to stop.
Resets the tick counter $0200, waits one tick and blanks the screen ($D011 = $0B).
Resets the tick counter $0200, waits one tick and turns the display on ($D011 bit 7 cleared, bit 4 set).

Start-up, from $095D. Stops CIA 1 timer A ($DC04-$DC05 = 0), sets CIA 2 timer A's high byte to 1 and enables its NMI ($DD0D = $81), clears CIA 1's control A ($DC0E = 0), runs the serial-port protection ($5F42, which also XORs $BA0A-$BA6A through $A949), the multiplexer (mux_init), CIA 2's NMI timer (nmi_timer_init) and the raster interrupt (irq_init); then fills its own first 40 bytes ($B9C3-$B9EA) with $20, CLI and JMP $F000 (main_entry). Runs once.

Unused: 18 bytes nothing reaches: LDA #$90 / STA $DD0E / LAX $BA64 / LDY #$00 / NOP $AD / JSR $A949 / LAX $BA63 (the LAX and two-byte NOP are undocumented opcodes), running on into protection_check_plain: an entry that would XOR that block with $A949 and then run it.

97 bytes ($BA0A-$BA6A) that start-up XORs once with $A71A-$A77A ($A949, called from $5F51). In the image as loaded they are plain code; the XOR turns them into noise, the state in play (play-ram matches entry XOR key, apart from $BA65). The plain code: a serial-port check like $5F57-$5F83 but longer: pulses CIA 1 timer A ($DC0E = $D9) and waits for its flag, 16 and then 16 times more, testing the serial-port flag ($DC0D bit 3, kept in $BA65) after each run, then shifts $DC0C out and waits three more times; any failure sets $0944 = 1 (tested at $A2CB, which then calls $A523) and $BA65 = 1; every exit is JMP $A949 (XOR again). Nothing calls it in this build.
Byte inside the XORed block: $00 in the image; the protection at $5F5F stores $DC0D's value here ($09 on VICE) after the block has been XORed, and the plain code at $BA12 would keep the same there.

From here to $BFFF (1,429 bytes, labelled old_build_*): an earlier assembly of the $F7xx-$FFxx code, placed lower, never run and not referenced. Chars $ED-$EF ($CF68-$CF7F): the open exit's pattern, copied over chars $E8-$EA by $A428.

Main entry. Reached from the start-up's JMP $F000 ($B9F5), from game over ($9BDD) and when a key or fire ends the attract mode ($957C). Port A of CIA 1 output with $7F (keyboard row 7), port B input; sprites off; current player $0938 = 0; sound silenced ($2690); $D016 = $18; variables cleared ($F6FA). Shows the title and waits for a key or fire (title_screen $B4C4, which jumps to the attract mode at $9500 instead when the title tune ends untouched); volume $1F; screen blanked ($B9A2); input menu and story (input_menu $B557); title picture again with tune 5 and the intro animation ($06D1); waits for the tune ($F70C); virtual sprite 8 at Y $70, three calls to $272F (X = 0, 1, 2), then animates the title sprite ($B983) once a tick until tune $3417 reports finished. Then blanks the screen, points the multiplexer's sprite-pointer stores back at page $C3 ($F976, $FC17; the intro used the bitmap bank), all sprites multicolour and on, stack reset (TXS with X = $FF), new game set up (new_game_init $F1B7) and JMP $957F, the main game loop. The LDA #$7F at $F08E is overwritten at once and has no effect.

Converts A + 1 (A = 0-98) to two decimal digits by repeated subtraction of 10: returns A = units (0-9) and X = tens. Used by draw_round_numbers, so the 0-based round shows as 1 upwards.

Draws the current player's round from the layouts at $8000: redraws the round numbers, then pointer ($11) = $8000 + round x 160 (round = $093D,X, 0-based, X = current player $0938; round x 32 + round x 128 built by shifts at $F3DA-$F40C) and falls into draw_wall. Called from new_game_init and $96CE (each round start). For the round index $20 (Doh) the pointer would be $9400.

Draws a wall from the 160-byte layout at ($11): 16 rows of 10 bytes. Each row: a 2-byte column mask, first bit first (14 columns used), then 8 bytes of 4-bit brick types (16 nibbles, unpacked to $0264-$0273). For each set bit, at row 1 + r, columns 1 + 2c and 2 + 2c of $C000: a type below 8 is a normal brick, screen codes $80 $81, colour RAM = type + 8, and $0455 (bricks left to clear) + 1; a type of 8 or more is special: type AND 3 = 1 a silver brick (codes $85 $89, counted in $0455, hit counter = silver_hits_by_round + 1), any other a gold brick (codes $8D $91, counter $80, not counted). Each special brick takes the next entry (from 1) of $0300 (flag $80), $0355 (hit counter) and $03AA/$03AB (its screen address); $0456 counts them. Every brick also shades the two cells one row down and one column right (OR $10 into the screen code; the second only if it is not a brick).

Silver-brick hit counter minus 1, by round (index $093D, 32 entries for rounds 1-32): 1 for rounds 1-8, 2 for 9-16, 3 for 17-24, 4 for 25-32. draw_wall stores the value + 1 in $0355; $ABA6 counts it down and silver_brick_hit ($B073) breaks the brick when it is zero.
Colour RAM value of the playfield background, by round AND 3: $0E, $0A, $0E, $0A (stored in $0457 by draw_playfield_background).

Fills the playfield (rows 1-24, columns 1-26) with the round's background pattern. The tile is 4 x 4 characters: screen code = $0458 + (row AND 3) x 4 + (column AND 3) cycling, colour $0457 (both by round AND 3, $F54A/$F54E). Then $0277-$0279 = $A3E8 + (round AND 3) and $D022 = $0C. Called from new_game_init, $96C8 and $9C20.

The five command bytes of the title percussion script ($20, $40, $60, $49, $4C), searched by drum_script_step at $FF01; the index found selects the handler from drum_command_lo ($F8A8) and drum_command_hi ($B47B): $A449, $A932, $A1E6, $A7C9, $A44E.
The playfield's top wall: 28 screen codes for row 0, columns 0-27 ($FB corner, $FC wall, $EB $EC $EB at 6-8 and $FD $FE $FD at 19-21, $FF corner), drawn by draw_walls.
Clears the variable page $0200-$02FF and the Y positions of the 12 virtual sprites ($942D-$9438; Y = 0 means unused). Called from main_entry and new_game_init.
Loops until $3417 returns zero (the tune that is playing has finished). Called from main_entry and $95CF, $9656, $96FF, $9BC3.
Unused: 7 bytes ($00 $00 $03 $02 $00 $0C $0F) that nothing reads, in the same shape as play_screen_colours after it; perhaps an earlier palette. Not known.
Colours for $D020-$D026 on the menu, story and play screens, copied by $B54D: border $00, background $00, extra backgrounds $0C, $0E, $00, sprite multicolours $01 and $0E.

Raster interrupt at line $F7 (247), the last of the frame. Acknowledges, sets the next interrupt to irq_frame_top ($F75E) at line $14 (20), counts the frame in $0201/$0241 (16 bits), CLI, then sorts the virtual sprites (mux_sort $FA06), finds how many are in use (mux_count_active $F7EB) and copies the tables for the next frame (mux_copy_tables $F7CD); hardware sprites 0 and 1 take their X from $9439 and $943A.

Raster interrupt at line $14 (20). Acknowledges, loads CIA 2 timer B with $07A8 and starts it one-shot ($DD0F = $19), so nmi_frame_a ($F855) fires some 30 lines later; sets the next raster interrupt to irq_mux ($FBEE) and places the first six virtual sprites (mux_first_six $F95F).
A single $00 between the IRQ code and the screen row address table at $F78B; nothing reads or runs it.

Start address of each screen row, as words: $C000 + 40 x row for rows 0-24 (50 bytes, $F78B-$F7BC). Read as low byte $F78B,Y and high byte $F78C,Y with Y = 2 x row by the text printers (print_menu_text $B635 and others) and by $0629, $A246, $A279, $A6D5, $AE1E, $AE88.
The same table seen one byte on: screen_row_addresses + 1, the high byte of row Y/2's address when read as $F78C,Y.
Unused: 16 bytes nothing reads: $FE $FD $FB $F7 $EF $DF $BF $7F (each bit cleared) then $01 $02 $04 ... $80 (each bit set). The same 16 bytes stand again at $FC81.

Copies the 12 virtual sprites' Y ($942D to $9421), X ($9445 to $9439) and sorted order ($9415 to $9409), so the interrupts during the next frame work from a fixed copy. Called from irq_frame_bottom and mux_init.
Six bit masks $20 $10 $08 $04 $02 $01, read by $AEFB.
Finds the last entry of the sorted order $9415 whose sprite has a non-zero Y (searching from entry 11 down), and leaves its index in $04, where the multiplexer starts. Y = 0 marks a slot as unused.
A second RTS straight after mux_count_active's own; nothing jumps to it.

Sets up the sprite multiplexer: the sorted order $9415 = 0-11, the positions of hardware sprites 0-5 zeroed ($D000-$D00B), then sort, copy and count (falls into mux_count_active). Called by the start-up ($B9E1) and the attract mode ($9500).

Colour of each of the 12 virtual sprites (slots 0-11, $F819-$F824), written to $D029+n when the slot is placed on hardware sprite 2+n (mux_first_six $F96B, irq_mux $FC0C). Slot 0 here: set to 2 by new_game_init.

Shape (sprite pointer) of each of the 12 virtual sprites (slots 0-11, $F825-$F830), written to $C3FA+n (or the page patched in at $F976/$FC17) with the slot's position. Slot 0 here: written by $07C3, $9B4C, $A40B, $A5DC and $AD9C.

Shape (sprite pointer) of virtual sprite slot 3 (role not traced here), copied to the pointer at $C3FA+n when placed; written by $0923.

Shape (sprite pointer) of virtual sprite slot 8 (title animation and aim_at_vaus X = 0), copied to the pointer at $C3FA+n when placed; written by $074C, $07BE, $08B3, $08BD, $08C3 and title_sprite_animate ($B992).
Shape (sprite pointer) of virtual sprite slot 10 (aim_at_vaus X = 2 (not checked)), copied to the pointer at $C3FA+n when placed; written by $0770.

Arms the raster interrupt chain: SEI, IRQ vector $FFFE = $F720 (irq_frame_bottom), raster interrupt enabled ($D01A = 1), CIA 1 timer A interrupt switched off ($DC0D = $01) and acknowledged, $01 = $35, multiplexer hardware-sprite counter $08 = 5, first raster line $F9. Called by the start-up ($B9E7) and the attract mode ($9506).

NMI handler while the vector holds $F855, fired by CIA 2 timer B. If the serial-port flag is set it goes to the never-run path at $F90B. Otherwise, first call of the pair ($F958 = 0): reloads timer B with $24F8 and restarts it, sets $F958 = 1 and runs the sound (sound_tick $F889). Second call ($F958 = 1, $F8AD): counts the tick in $0200 (waited on by wait_tick $B472), runs down $0216 (or, when $0217 = 2, clears it once the tune has ended), hides hardware sprites 2-7 (Y = 0), repairs the raster chain if it is still on irq_mux (vector $FBEE: forces $F720), sets the NMI vector to nmi_frame_end ($F903), and runs the sound again when $0209 = 0 (during play: twice per frame).

Sound for one NMI: CLI; while $0209 bit 7 is set (the title screen) steps the percussion script (drum_script_step $FEF4); then calls the sound driver's seven routines $2B5D, $2C15, $2D6C, $2EC5, $3022, $3160 and $32D2.
Low bytes of the title percussion script's command handlers, in the order of drum_script_commands ($F6D9); high bytes at drum_command_hi ($B47B). Copied into the JSR at $FF12.

nmi_frame_a's second call of the pair: ticks $0200, runs down $0216 (when $0217 = 2, clears it only once tune $3417 has ended), hides hardware sprites 2-7 (Y = 0 at $D005-$D00F), forces the raster chain back to irq_frame_bottom if the vector is still on irq_mux (low byte $EE; never seen in the simulator), points the NMI vector at nmi_frame_end ($F903) and, during play ($0209 = 0), runs sound_tick a second time.

NMI handler while the vector holds $F903 (late in the frame). If CIA 2's serial-port flag is set ($F90B, never run in the simulator): reads $DD0C, sets timer A to 2, masks CIA 2's interrupts, starts timer A with the serial port as output ($DD0E = $51), waits, writes the byte back to $DD0C, SEI and JMP $0107 (the stack page, where the fast loader ran); what that path is for is not known. Otherwise: NMI vector back to nmi_frame_a ($F855), timer B high byte 9, started one-shot ($DD0F = $19), $F958 = 0.
Which half of the nmi_frame_a pair comes next: 0 the first (reload timer, sound), 1 the second (tick). Cleared by nmi_frame_end.
Delay counts for drum_85 ($B290), one per outer step (Y = 5-0): $23 $14 $0C $09 $06 $03.

Places the first virtual sprites of the frame, called from irq_frame_top: from sorted entry $04 downward, each slot's colour, shape, X and Y go to hardware sprite 2 + $08 ($08 counting 5 to 0, position registers from mux_sprite_offsets $FC7B). After six, or if none remain, it sets the raster for the next slot's Y - 14 (if below $F0) and leaves the chain on irq_mux; when the list ends it sets raster $F7 and the vector to irq_frame_bottom.

Operand high byte of mux_first_six's STA $C3FA,Y: the page of the sprite pointers ($C3 for the screen at $C000). Main_entry stores $C3 here after the intro, which had pointed it at the bitmap bank's $63F8.

Unused code (nothing calls it, never run in the simulator): LDY #0, adds the 32 bytes at a self-modified pointer (operand $F9C3-$F9C4, starting $9500) into $0454, moves the pointer on 32 bytes; when it reaches $A600, compares the sum with $09: equal, restarts at $9500 with the sum cleared; different, sets $0944 = 1 (the flag that $A2CB tests and answers with $A523). Then JMP $F9FD to itself, and the stray bytes $8D $FF $0F $2C $00 $DE. A checksum of $9500-$A5FF left out of this build.

Insertion sort of the virtual sprites' order list $9415 (12 entries) by Y ($942D), largest first, so the multiplexer can walk it from the end (topmost sprite) upward; $0B counts the moves. Called from irq_frame_bottom and mux_init.

Shows both players' lives ($0936, $0937, BCD) in the panel at $C1B5-$C1B6 (row 10) and $C31D-$C31E (row 19): a tens digit of 0 or 9 shows as a blank ($1C), and $99 (no player) as two blanks. Called from new_game_init, draw_side_panel, check_extra_life and $9C0D, $A894.

Extra life: compares the current player's score ($0927-$0929 or $092A-$092C) with the threshold ($092D-$092F or $0930-$0932, BCD); when it is reached, adds $20 to the threshold's middle byte (another 20000 on the screen), adds 1 to the player's lives (BCD; not stored if the result would be $88 or more), sets $0216 = $28 and $0217 = 2, starts tune $2F ($262B) and redraws the lives.

Checks for an extra life, then copies the current player's score into the high score $0941-$0943 if it is higher, and prints the high score ($C0BF, row 4), player 1's score ($C187, row 9) and player 2's ($C2EF, row 18) as six digits each (the panel adds a fixed last 0). Every 8 frames ($0201 bit 3) it flips the colour of the current player's marker beside the panel ($D8EF for player 1, $DA57 for player 2; the other set to $0E). Called from the main loop ($95B7) and $9560, $962E, draw_side_panel.

Adds the 3-byte BCD amount in $0933-$0935 to the current player's score ($0927-$0929, or $092A-$092C for player 2) in decimal mode and clears the amount. Called from brick_hit ($B28A) and $9F4A, $9F5B, $A9E0.

Raster interrupt of the sprite multiplexer, chained between irq_frame_top and irq_frame_bottom. For each next slot in sorted order whose Y - 14 the beam has reached: colour, shape, X and Y onto the next hardware sprite (2-7 in turn). When the next slot's line is still ahead it sets the raster interrupt there (or, if the line has already passed, one line on); when the list ends or the line is $F0 or more, the chain goes on to irq_frame_bottom at line $F7.
Operand high byte of irq_mux's STA $C3FA,Y: the page of the sprite pointers, $C3; main_entry rewrites it with $C3 after the intro.
Unused: 7 bytes of code that nothing reaches (DEC $04 / BMI +3 / JMP $FBF9), the same as irq_mux's loop end; left over from editing.

irq_mux's ending: the sprite list is done (or the next line is $F0 or more): counter $08 = 5, $04 = $0B, and unless the vector is already $F720 sets raster line $F7 and the vector to irq_frame_bottom. Then the shared exit (pull registers, RTI), and at $FC72 the case where the next sprite's line has already passed: $D012 + 1 so the interrupt comes again on the next line.
Offsets of the position registers of hardware sprites 2-7 from $D000: $04 $06 $08 $0A $0C $0E, indexed by the multiplexer's counter $08.
Unused: 16 bytes nothing reads, the same clear-bit and set-bit masks as at $F7BD.
Eight bit masks $80 $40 $20 $10 $08 $04 $02 $01, read by $A4E0 and $A4FE.

Reads the chosen input device and moves the Vaus, unless $023D is set (then it returns at once). Called from the main loop ($958D), $9604 and the menu ($B5AC). The device routine (read_input_device) gives the fire state in A, stored in $0236 (1 = pressed), and for joystick, keyboard and mouse a step in X (positive = left) that is added to the Vaus centre $0206, held between 0 and 255; paddles set $0206 themselves (read_paddle_entry). Then place_vaus.

Jumps to the reader of the input device in $093F through an RTS: pushes the address from input_reader_hi/lo minus one. 0 Neos mouse ($FE43), 1 joystick ($FDA2), 2 keyboard ($FD7B), 3 paddles ($FCB3), the order of the menu's N J K P.
Low bytes, minus one, of the input readers in device order: $42 $A1 $7A $B2 (mouse $FE43, joystick $FDA2, keyboard $FD7B, paddles $FCB3).
High bytes of the input readers in device order: $FE $FD $FD $FC (read_input_device pushes these first).

Paddles (device 3): drops the return into read_input_move_vaus (PLA PLA), reads the paddle (read_paddle $FE09), stores fire in $0236 and the new Vaus centre in $0206 directly, then place_vaus, whose RTS returns to read_input_move_vaus's caller.
Delay counts for drum_84 ($B500), one per outer step (Y = 5-0): $05 $1E $19 $14 $0F $0A.

Keeps the Vaus between the walls and sets its sprites: with centre $0206 and half-width $020A, the left edge is held at $20 or more and the right edge below $DB (reaching it sets $023E = 1), $0206 is corrected, and the Vaus's two sprite X positions are written to $9445 (left) and $9446 (left + 2 x half-width). Also stores zero through the self-modified STX at $FCF6 (to $150C at first; this routine then points it at $1515), an address nothing reads. Called from read_input_move_vaus and $9530, $9B02.
Operand low byte of place_vaus's STX at $FCF6: $0C in the image (STX $150C), set to $15 (STX $1515) by $FD52 and $FD71. Neither address is read anywhere; the dead code at $0960 also writes here.
Six bytes read by $ACE2 (Y = 0-5): $28 $0A $14 $0A $0F $0A. Their meaning belongs to that routine.

Keyboard (device 2): left SHIFT (key $0F) sets the left bit, right SHIFT (key $34) the right bit of $0203 (through key_held $0832); fire is $DC01 bit 4 with keyboard row 7 left selected by key_held: SPACE, or fire on a joystick in port 1. Then joystick_step ($FDBF) with Y = 1.

Joystick (device 1): reads port 1 ($DC01), or port 2 ($DC00) for player 2 when two devices are chosen ($0940 = 1). The five low bits, inverted, go to $0203 (bit 0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right, 4 fire), then joystick_step.

Turns the direction bits in $0203 into the Vaus's step: left and right together, or neither, give X = 0; left X = 2 x ($023A + 1), 4 when $023A = 0; right the same, negated. Then A = 1 if the fire bit of $DC00,Y (the port being read) is low, else 0.

Reads the paddle of the current player ($0938): $DC00 = $5F (port A's top bits 01: a paddle pair to the SID), fire from $DC01 (bit 2 for player 1, bit 3 for player 2, paddle_fire_bits) as A = 0 or 1, position from $D419 (player 1) or $D41A (player 2): X = (255 - value + $0206) / 2, half way from the old centre to the reading.
The paddle fire bit in $DC01 for each player: $04, $08.
Bit ORed into the mouse's port data at $FE5C, by port index X: $80 for port A ($DC00), $40 for port B ($DC01).
Delay counts for drum_82 ($F345), one per outer step (Y = 13-0): $20 $10 $08 $04 $02 $01 $28 $0A $3C $0A $14 $0A $20 $40.

Neos mouse (device 0): port 1 (X = 1, $DC01), or port 2 (X = 0) for player 2 with two devices. Sets bit 4 of the port to output, then reads four nibbles, toggling bit 4 between them with short delays (delay_y $FEC9): the high and low nibble of the X movement (X), then of the Y movement (Y). Button: A = 1 when $D419 reads $FF. Note: TAX at $FE86 replaces the port index with the X movement, so the later reads and writes $DC00,X land on CIA 1 register (movement AND 15), not on the mouse's port; see the report.
Delay of Y x 7 cycles (NOP, DEY, BNE), used between the mouse's nibbles.
Delay counts for drum_81 ($F604), one per outer step (Y = 5-0): $40 $1E $3E $19 $3C $14.
Unused: 11 bytes of code nothing reaches: LDA #$01 / STA $D015 / STA $D027 / JMP $957F. The old build at $BF63 has the same lines ending JMP $94C5.
The mouse reader's high nibble, kept while the low one is read (written $FE6E and $FE9B, ORed in at $FE83 and $FEB0).

Plays the title percussion: if a sound is due ($DF non-zero) it clears $DF, calls the drum routine through the JSR at $FEE8 (operand set by drum_script_step) and sets the volume to $0F OR $3FFF. Called only by the title loop ($B4E0), so the drums play on the title screen only.
Low byte of the JSR at $FEE8, the drum routine to call: set from $B07D + drum ($FF2D).
High byte of the JSR at $FEE8: set from $A253 + drum ($FF33).

Steps the title percussion script, from sound_tick while $0209 bit 7 is set: counts $DC down; at zero reads the script at ($DA) (start $9A71, set by $B52C). A byte below $80 is a command: found in drum_script_commands and called through the JSR at $FF12 (it reads its own operands and moves ($DA)), then the next byte is read. A byte of $80 or more is a drum: it goes to $DF (played by drum_play), the next byte to $DC (the wait), ($DA) moves on 2, and the JSR at $FEE8 is pointed at that drum's routine. A command byte not in the table would run the search on past it.
Low byte of the JSR at $FF12, the script command's handler (from drum_command_lo).
High byte of the JSR at $FF12 (from drum_command_hi at $B47B).

Unused to $FFF9 (nothing reads or runs it): $FF3A-$FF5D is a copy of drum_script_step's last lines assembled for other addresses (it patches $FF0D-$FF0E); from $FF5E data: $ED $EF ... $FF $01 $23 ... $EF, $55 $55 $55, runs of $FF, and graphic-looking bytes ($AA, $A8, $C0, $3A, $0E). Left over from the build.

Part of the unused tail: 156 bytes ($FF5E-$FFF9) nothing reads: a run of odd bytes $ED-$FF, nibble pairs $01 $23 $45 $67 $89 $AB $CD $EF, $55 x3, $FF fill, then bytes that look like sprite or character rows.

The hardware NMI vector, owned by the game with the KERNAL banked out ($01 = $35): $0000 in the image (not part of the loaded file), set to $F903 by nmi_timer_init and switched between $F855 and $F903 by the NMI handlers.
The RESET vector's RAM: $0000, never written or read by the game.
The hardware IRQ vector: $FFFF in the image, set to $F720 by irq_init and rewritten by each raster handler to the next ($F75E, $FBEE, $F720).
